messages.author: 07dfa576fa8795bf
messages.subject: Error in DSM
parts:
Hey,

I have some troubles to model with the dsm package. When I write the following code: 

mod1 <- dsm(N~s(x,y), detectionRS, segdataRS, obsdataRS, engine = "gam",
            convert.units = 1, family = quasipoisson(link = "log"), group = TRUE,
            gamma = 1.4, control = list(keepData = TRUE), availability = 1,
            strip.width = NULL, segment.area = NULL, weights = NULL, scale=-1)

I get this error:

Error in `[.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, , cluster.name) : 
  undefined columns selected

I compared my dataset with the dolphins data to make sure that all my columns were defined correctly as factors, numerical or integrer and that I had all the required ones. I don't understand why the error message is talking about cluster.name because I have no column with that name and it's not a prerequisite according to the package instruction. 

All help would be greatly appreciated and I'd be very grateful because I am totally blocked by this error. 

Thanks,
Julia

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in DSM
parts:
Julia:

Regarding the "cluster.name" error; by setting the argument "group=TRUE" you are estimating abundance/density of groups in your population, rather than abundance/density of individuals.  This is an unusual situation.  The dsm() functions presumes the existence of a field named "size" to indicate the size of each group detected.  I expect the absence of a field named "size" is what caused the error.

Regarding your previous question on area of prediction grid cells--for our demonstration (spotted dolphin) dsm project, we've used the ETOPO2v2 NOAA database.  With that database open in ArcGIS, you can examine the "area" property of the grid cells to determine prediction grid cell size for use with this bathymetry data.
